subject: Discovery Recap: Dedicated Capacity fit for FinApp — next steps
msg_1_subject: Discovery Recap: Dedicated Capacity fit for FinApp — next steps
msg_1_body:
Thanks again for the time today — really appreciated the detailed walkthrough of FinApp's production constraints. Below is a concise recap of the problems, success criteria, and proposed next steps so we can align internally and with your team.

Pain points we heard
- Unpredictable latency and cost spikes during peak windows (end of month reporting).
- Current multi-tenant hosting leads to noisy-neighbor latency variability and cold-starts that impact SLAs.
- Need strong data isolation and auditability for PII-sensitive flows.
- Current infra: models served via third-party hosting on AWS with autoscaling policies; model is a 13B Llama variant (quantized) with ~1.2B tokens/month.

Success criteria for a Dedicated fit
- Predictable baseline throughput: sustain ~150 TPS p50 with p95 latency target <200ms for core endpoints.
- Ability to burst to ~300 TPS for short windows (10–15 minutes) without degradation.
- Single-tenant isolation (no shared compute) and KMS integration for encryption at rest.
- Integration with SSO and audit logs for compliance.

What Redwood can provide (next items we discussed)
- Dedicated reserved GPU pools sized for baseline throughput + burst policy for short windows.
- Autoscaling and burst policy options with explicit cold-start behavior and KV cache sizing to avoid latency cliffs.
- Security/compliance intake + SOC2 artifacts and optional on-prem/private deployment paths.

Action items / proposed timeline
- Redwood: sizing + ballpark estimate (this PDF) and a short capacity model — aim to deliver by EOD Fri, 2026-02-27. [Attached: Redwood_Dedicated_Estimate_FinApp_2026-02-27.pdf]
- FinApp: confirm peak burst characteristics (duration, frequency) and whether PII appears in cache or only in logs — please reply with details.
- Schedule technical deep-dive with Connor (solutions) + Aditya (security/infra) to validate model compatibility and deployment topology — proposed Wed 2026-03-03 10:00 AM PT.

Please confirm if anything above is incorrect or missing. If Wed 3/3 doesn’t work, propose two other slots next week and we’ll prioritize.

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole | Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | (415) 555-0192

--

msg_2_subject: Re: Discovery Recap: Dedicated Capacity fit for FinApp — next steps
msg_2_body:
Thanks Marissa — helpful recap and appreciate the quick turnaround. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Peak numbers: baseline ~150 TPS for our main inference path; we see daily spikes but the major concern is end-of-month reports where traffic can spike to ~300 TPS for 8–12 minutes (happens 1–2 times/month).
- Model details: we currently run a quantized Llama-2 13B via Triton on AWS, with an internal caching layer in front (we cannot persist PII in that cache).
- Compliance: we need KMS integration and audit logs retained for 1 year. SOC2 documentation is a hard requirement for procurement.
- Contract horizon: we’re looking at a 12-month committed baseline if the numbers & SLA make sense.

We’d like to proceed with the technical deep-dive — Wed 3/3 10:00 AM PT works for Priya and me. Please include Connor + Aditya.

Oliver
Oliver Reed | Head of ML Engineering | FinApp
oliver.reed@finapp.com | +1 415-555-0124

msg_3_subject: Re: Discovery Recap: Dedicated Capacity fit for FinApp — estimate attached
msg_3_body:
Great — thanks for confirming Oliver. I’ve attached our initial sizing & estimate PDF (ballpark numbers) and a short spreadsheet capturing the input assumptions. Key notes: 

- Baseline sizing recommendation: 4x A100 80GB-equivalent nodes reserved to hit the ~150 TPS baseline with room for KV cache to reduce per-token compute.
- Burst plan: allow autoscale to add up to 8 nodes for short durations (configurable policy with warm cache pre-warming options).
- Security/compliance: Aditya will own the SOC2 artifact handoff and KMS integration plan; we’ll surface required controls and an audit log schema.

Attached: Redwood_Dedicated_Estimate_FinApp_2026-02-27.pdf, FinApp_requirements_MVP.xlsx

Next steps / owners:
- Marissa (Redwood): finalize estimate and send the DocuSign/quote once we align on commit length and topology (by 2026-03-01).
- Connor (Redwood): technical deep-dive to validate network topology, model binary compatibility, and KV cache sizing (meeting Wed 2026-03-03).
- Aditya (Redwood): prepare SOC2 artifacts + KMS integration overview ahead of the call.

Oliver/Priya — can you share the frequency distribution for spikes (daily/hourly) and confirm whether short-lived PII will be present in cache? That will materially affect cache TTLs and isolation strategy.

Thanks — looking forward to the call.

Marissa

msg_4_subject: Re: Discovery Recap: Dedicated Capacity fit for FinApp — internal sizing note
msg_4_body:
Internal: quick technical note ahead of Wed’s deep-dive. Based on the inputs so far I recommend we validate with the following starting point: 

- Reserved pool: 4x A100 80GB-equivalent (baseline). KV cache sized to hold ~20M tokens for hot prefixes to avoid repeated decode.
- Burst policy: scale to 8 nodes for up to 15 minutes; use warm standby instances and a short pre-warm hook triggered by traffic anomaly detection.
- Latency target: with warm cache we should be able to hit p95 <200ms for core endpoints; cold-start could add ~200–400ms depending on model shard placement — document mitigations.
- Cost ballpark (monthly reserved + burst buffer): see attached capacity_modeling_notes.csv — this is high level and will be updated after we validate exact model memory footprint and request mix.

I’ll own the deep-dive demo for model binary compatibility and KV cache tuning. Recommend we also ask FinApp to provide a small sample of live traffic traces (sanitized) to run an accurate capacity model.

Connor
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
connor@redwood.com
